Subject: Post-call recap: embeddings fit & pilot next steps

Hi Daniel / Priya 

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery + proposed next steps so we have alignment before the pilot: 

What we heard:
- Primary use case: semantic product search + "also viewed" / related items recommendations.
- Index size: ~3M SKUs currently (images + text fields) but you expect ~4-5M in 6 months.
- Query patterns: short product queries, SKU lookups, and some long natural language queries from customer support.
- Latency SLO: P95 <= 80ms for retrieval; P50 ideally < 20ms for site search.
- Privacy: PI-level data not allowed in third-party storage; you require SOC2 and KMS integration.

Model/fit focus we discussed:
- Candidate embeddings: open alternatives (e.g., all-MiniLM, SBERT variants) vs Redwood-curated text-embedding-3 models.
- Dimensionality: tradeoffs between 384/768/1536 dims for recall vs cost/latency.
- Drift/quality regression: want automated alerts and a clear way to quantify regressions after model updates.

Proposed next steps (pilot scope):
1) Redwood runs a fit validation on a 10k sample of your index and query set: compute MRR, Recall@10, and average cosine similarity distributions for candidate models.
2) Evaluate dimensionality tradeoffs: run 384 / 768 / 1536 dim variants and produce latency/cost estimates for host vs dedicated deployment.
3) Establish baseline drift metrics (centroid shift, retrieval stability on seed queries) and set thresholds for alerts.
4) Security review: sign and share an NDA + SOC2 excerpts; we will propose KMS config for Private/Dedicated options.

Deliverables (week 1-2):
- CSV with benchmark metrics across models (MRR, Recall@1/5/10, avg latency).
- Promptset and normalized query set (attached as promptset_v2.json & sample_queries_10k.csv).
- Short slide with recommended model (one recommended + one fallback) and cost/latency estimates.

Questions for you now:
- Can you share a 10k anonymized sample of product descriptions + representative query logs? (CSV okay; strip any customer PII).
- Any required PO or procurement steps we should prep for if the pilot looks good?

If that sounds right, I'll loop Marcus (ML) on a technical call this week to align on evaluation details and start the sample ingestion.

Thanks 
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Thanks Daniel 
 appreciate the fast turnaround on the sample. A few quick answers while we prep: 

- Cost sketch (very rough):
  - 1536-d embedding (hosted): ~0.0009 USD/embedding; dedicated nodes reduce per-embedding cost by ~30% at scale.
  - 768-d embedding (hosted): ~0.00045 USD/embedding.
  - 384-d (mini): ~0.0002 USD/embedding but expect lower recall on long-form queries.

- Regression detection plan (short):
  - Primary metrics: MRR and Recall@10 on a fixed eval query set.
  - Distribution monitoring: per-query delta in similarity score; flag when median delta > 0.03 cosine across seed queries.
  - Drift metric: centroid cosine shift on newest 10k embeddings vs baseline; alert when shift > 0.05.

I'm attaching the initial benchmark CSV (semantic_search_benchmarks_v1.csv) with a placeholder example and the promptset file I mentioned. Marcus will propose an evaluation script; he can also give more detail about dimensionality tradeoffs.

Hey team 
 quick technical notes and proposed evaluation script steps from my side: 

1) Evaluation plan (executable):
- Ingest your 10k sample (text fields only) and the 2k representative queries.
- Compute embeddings for candidate models: text-embedding-3-large (1536), text-embedding-3-small (768), and a cost-optimized SBERT mini (384).
- Build an HNSW index (efConstruction 200, M=16) for each embedding set and run standard retrieval.
- Metrics: MRR, Recall@1/5/10, avg retrieval latency (cold cache & warm cache), index size, and per-query similarity distributions.

2) Dimensionality tradeoffs:
- 1536: best recall on long queries and paraphrase instances; index size ~4x of 384 dims, vectors take more memory and slower cold-cache.
- 768: reasonable middle ground, good fit for mixed queries; ~2x memory of 384.
- 384: fastest and cheapest but expect ~6-8% absolute Recall@10 degradation on complex NL queries in our prior retail benchmarks.

3) Drift/regression detection details:
- Baseline: compute per-query top-k stability (Jaccard over top-10) and per-query similarity delta.
- Drift alert thresholds: centroid shift > 0.05 OR median per-query similarity drop > 0.03 triggers an incident ticket to your product quality channel.
- Automated daily job: compute these metrics on a rolling 7-day window; we can expose them in Redwood Console and push alerts to Slack/PagerDuty.

4) Resource estimates (pilot 10k):
- Embedding compute: ~0.5 GPU-hours for 10k at 1536 on a single A100-ish node.
- Index build: ~20-30 minutes; memory ~8-12GB per 10k for 1536-d vectors in HNSW.

5) Security notes: we support bring-your-own-KMS and Private deployment (VPC)  we can provide SOC2 excerpts and a short architecture diagram for ingestion without leaving your network.

I attached a small script snippet and the CSV we'll output format for metrics. Next steps: once we get your sample, I'll run the three models and share a short notebook + CSV of benchmarks.

-Marcus
